stemMd: Why were important alerts sometimes missed?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They were buried among many routine messages.

options.label: B
options.textMd: All engineers refused to read any messages.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The team had no software running.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The channel contained only urgent messages.

explanationMd: The first paragraph identifies alert overload: many low-value messages obscured significant warnings. The problem was not complete absence of failure reporting but difficulty noticing it within the volume.

distractorRationale.b: The passage describes overload, not a universal refusal.
distractorRationale.c: The system monitored active software events.
